chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who prayed two rak'at in a garment in which there was major ritual impurity, then he came to know of it, he (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him is that he re-commences the prayer.'

He (the narrator) said: 'And I asked him about a man who prayed and in his garment was major ritual impurity or blood, until he finished his prayer, then he came to know.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'His prayer has passed, and there is nothing upon him.'

key_terms.لَا شَيْ‏ءَ عَلَيْهِ: There is nothing upon him (no penalty or re-performance required)

ai.seo_question: Does a prayer become invalid if ritual impurity is found on the clothing after the prayer is finished?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the ruling on *salat* validity when ritual impurity (*janabah*) or blood is present on clothing, distinguishing between discovery before completion versus after. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that if the impurity is known only after the prayer is finished, the prayer is valid (*qad matat*), reflecting the principle that doubt does not negate certainty. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the state of purity at the time of prayer's completion rather than requiring immediate correction if the error was unknown.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus Bin Abdul Rahman, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws regarding a man who prays two Rak’at (Rak’ats) of Salāt in a cloth wherein is a sexual impurity, then he comes to know of it. Heasws said: ‘Upon him is that he re-commences the Salāt’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘And I asked himasws about a man who prays Salāt and in his cloth is a sexual impurity, or blood, until he is free from his Salāt, then he comes to know’. Heasws said: ‘His Salāt has passed, and there is nothing upon him’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman from ibn Muskan from abu Basir who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who performs two Rak‘at Salah (prayer) wearing clothes in which one has experienced sexual relation, then he comes to know it. He (the Imam) said, ‘He is required to perform it from the beginning.’

He (the narrator) has said that he then asked him (the Imam) about one who performs Salah (prayer) wearing clothes in which sexual relation is experienced or there is blood in it. He completes his Salah (prayer) then he comes to know it. He (the Imam) said, ‘His Salah (prayer) is passed. He is not required to perform it again.”’
